LMP3.title: RLR MSport win again as Eurointernational lose the lead to an electrical fault
LMP3.dek: Farano, van Uitert and Garofall won for RLR MSport by about five seconds over the Ecurie Ecosse/Nielsen Ligier after Eurointernational’s late electrical problem, taking the LMP3 points lead.

facts.v: AT Racing’s Jensen set the quickest LMP3 lap, 1:26.408, but it was deleted for track limits, handing pole to Lahaye’s Ultimate Norma on 1:26.519.

chapters.title: Late changes up and down the class
text: Round three of the European Le Mans Series brought LMP3 to Austria with Eurointernational’s #11 leading the standings and RLR MSport, winners of an earlier round, the closest challenger. RLR’s crew had a lucky charm for the weekend, each driver painting a fingernail for good luck, with Garofall joking that it was van Uitert’s idea.

The paddock was full of late driver changes. DKR Engineering’s all-Silver line-up was gone: the Toril brothers had decided not to finish the season and Glorieux was injured, so Sanchez, Enqvist and Lavergne took over the #8 Norma for what was described as a one-race deal. Inter Europol’s #14 Ligier added the Bronze-rated Belotti, and M. Racing - YMR called up 62-year-old Alain Ferté, a 14-time Le Mans starter, to replace Ferrer in its #19 Norma. Ecurie Ecosse/Nielsen ran in a simplified blue-and-white livery, and United Autosports’ #2, the only all-American line-up in the series, was driven by 2017 class champions Rayhall and Falb.

Ultimate’s Lahaye led the first practice session on 1:26.927, with United’s Bell within two hundredths and the #19 Norma third. The #12 Eurointernational Ligier was black-flagged and then reported to the stewards for a breach of black-flag procedure, which limited the car to 11 laps. Second practice was damp, and van Uitert’s 1:27.176 in the #15 RLR Ligier topped the order ahead of the #19 Norma.

chapters.title: Jensen’s pole lap is deleted
text: The ten-minute session ended with the order reshuffling constantly. Jensen put AT Racing’s #9 Ligier on top with a 1:26.408, just over a tenth clear of Lahaye’s Ultimate Norma, but the lap was deleted for exceeding track limits. With his next best of 1:26.960 Jensen dropped to sixth in the class, and pole went to Lahaye’s 1:26.519 in the #17.

Légeret was second for M. Racing - YMR on 1:26.583 with a late effort, ahead of van Uitert’s #15 RLR Ligier on 1:26.703 and Borga’s #4 COOL Racing Ligier on 1:26.751. Sanchez was fifth in the re-crewed DKR Norma on 1:26.917, so the top six were separated by less than half a second.

chapters.title: RLR in front, trouble behind
text: RLR’s #15 led most of the race and gave up the position only during the pit cycles, which kept it in front through the opening half. Ferté’s #19 Norma was part of the leading group for a time before trouble intervened; it covered 112 laps and was not classified.

In the second hour the #10 Oregon Team Norma was involved in a three-car collision at Turn 4 with an LMP2 Dallara and an IDEC Oreca, which brought out a full-course yellow. Oregon eventually finished 16 laps down on the class winner.

chapters.title: Noble closes in, then the safety car
text: Short, at times sharp, showers arrived from the third hour. During Farano’s stint, RLR’s lead of more than a minute was cut to 14 seconds by Noble in the Ecurie Ecosse/Nielsen Ligier #7. A late safety car erased what was left of the margin and the field was bunched up.

Eurointernational’s #11 gained most from the neutralisation and went into the final stint at the front, but the car then had to pit with an electrical problem. That returned the lead to RLR with Garofall back in the car. Hippe in Inter Europol’s #13 and Kapadia in the #7 were left fighting over second, with Hippe putting in what was described as a stunning run.

chapters.title: Kapadia gets the better of Hippe
text: Garofall brought the RLR Ligier home 5.092 seconds clear of Kapadia, who had got past Hippe to take second for Ecurie Ecosse/Nielsen. Hippe’s #13 completed the podium on the same lap, with Ultimate’s #17 Norma fourth also on the lead lap.

chapters.title: RLR take the points lead
text: The #15 won on 148 laps, with the Ecurie Ecosse/Nielsen #7, Inter Europol’s #13 and Ultimate’s #17 all completing the same distance. AT Racing’s #9 was fifth, one lap down on 147, ahead of the NEFIS Ligier #5 in sixth and the delayed Eurointernational #11 in seventh. Jensen’s 1:27.757 in the #9 was the fastest lap of the class. The #19 Norma and United’s #2 Ligier, which stopped after 70 laps, were not classified.

It was a second win of the season for van Uitert, Farano and Garofall, and it lifted RLR MSport past the Eurointernational crew at the top of the standings with three rounds remaining. Van Uitert said he planned to buy more lucky nail polish, although the drivers might need something new, adding that his early lead had let team-mates manage the rest. The series moves on to Silverstone in August.

LMGTE.title: Proton’s Porsche leads from the first lap to win a six-car GTE class
LMGTE.dek: Gianluca Roda, Giorgio Roda and Cairoli won for Proton Competition from the opening lap, with Spirit of Race second and Ebimotors third after Proton’s sister car took a late penalty for track limits.

facts.v: Molina’s 1:28.827 gave JMW Motorsport its first pole since the Hungaroring in 2013 and the first for a Ferrari 488 GTE this season.

chapters.title: Six GTE cars and a Porsche reunion
text: Only six cars made up the GTE class in Austria: Ferraris from JMW Motorsport, Spirit of Race and Krohn Racing, and Porsche 911 RSRs from Proton Competition (two cars) and Ebimotors. Proton’s Cairoli and Olsen rejoined the team’s line-ups after missing the previous round, and Ebimotors added American Bret Curtis as its third driver, who confirmed he would stay for the rest of the season.

Ebimotors was running a Porsche leased from Proton and this was its last race with that chassis; the team planned to collect a newer car from Proton’s base on 27 July ahead of Silverstone. JMW’s Ferrari returned to its traditional yellow livery after running in white at Le Mans.

JMW led the first practice session through Molina’s 1:28.829, more than half a second faster than Proton’s #88 in second, with Bertolini’s Krohn Ferrari third. Second practice was wet, and Griffin put the Spirit of Race Ferrari on top with a 1:29.845 ahead of Proton’s #77.

chapters.title: Molina takes pole by 0.098s
text: Molina put the JMW Ferrari #66 on pole with a 1:28.827, a first pole for the team since the Hungaroring in 2013 and the first for a Ferrari 488 GTE in the championship this season. He said he tried to find clear track, which was not hard with six cars, and that the team had not fitted new tyres during the session, unlike Bertolini and Cairoli.

Cairoli led for a time and ended up second for Proton’s #88 on 1:28.925, 0.098 behind. A late flier took Bertolini up to third in the Krohn Ferrari #83 on 1:28.967. Griffin lost most of his quick laps in the Spirit of Race #55 to track limits and was fourth on 1:29.190, ahead of Olsen’s Proton #77 and Pera’s Ebimotors #80. All six cars were within six tenths of a second.

chapters.title: Roda passes the pole-sitter at the start
text: Giorgio Roda got the #88 Porsche past pole-sitter Liam Griffin’s JMW Ferrari at the start and opened up an early gap of about ten seconds. That lead then grew and shrank through five full-course yellows and a single safety car period.

JMW and Spirit of Race had been fighting over second in the first hour, but MacDowall’s JMW stopped on track at Turn 7 on an out-lap with a gearbox problem, ending the car’s race after 43 laps. It was not classified.

chapters.title: Second place swaps between the Ferrari and the Porsche
text: With JMW out, second place changed hands repeatedly between Spirit of Race’s #55 Ferrari, driven by Cameron, Griffin and Scott, and Proton’s #77 Porsche of Ried, Dienst and Olsen. Only in the final hour, with Matt Griffin in the Ferrari, did the #55 pull clear to secure second place.
Krohn’s #83 Ferrari ran at the back of the class and would be classified fifth.

chapters.title: The #77 loses a podium to a penalty
text: Cairoli took over for the last stint of the #88 and kept the Spirit of Race Ferrari at a safe distance to complete the win. In the closing minutes the #77 was given a drive-through for repeated track-limit abuse, and Ebimotors’ Porsche, with Babini, Pera and Curtis, went past to take third.

chapters.title: Proton’s Porsche win follows Le Mans
text: The #88 won on 147 laps, with Spirit of Race’s #55 second and Ebimotors’ #80 third, both on 146. Proton’s #77 finished fourth on 145 and Krohn’s #83 fifth on 143. JMW’s #66, the pole-sitter, was not classified after 43 laps. Cairoli set the class fastest lap, 1:29.517.

It was Porsche’s first ELMS win of the season and the second in a row for the 911 RSR after Proton’s class win at Le Mans, the first for the latest-spec car in the series. Cairoli said the team deserved it and that the car had been a pleasure to drive. The next round is at Silverstone in August.
